title: Flowing Memories
subtitle: The world shifts under observation. Memories are but echoes in a glass tank.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: As you can see, this is the toybox's core.
The core is contained within a metallic frame. At its center, something between a cloud of fog and a jellyfish envelops matter and symbols too strange to name.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: After running it through some preliminary tests, we discovered its inner contents don't match up with any known arcane material.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Our next step would be to record and analyze its center.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But there's a problem. The matter and symbols floating in the core seem to change their state every time we observe it.
Without warning, the interior shifts again. Two forms slowly emerge from the "fog."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Are those gears?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hmm. I think it looks more like the black and white grid of a crossword puzzle.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Adler, your observation right now—the observation of a cryptographer with very distinct interests and inclinations ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: Has become a new influencing factor on the core.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I understand. Under these circumstances, analyzing its contents is pointless.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Precisely. But the problems don't stop there.
Ulrich gestures toward the toybox on the table.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Within the three-hour period after the core's removal, the environment in the toybox descended into chaos. Understandably so.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The core has an "unmeasurable" quality; it stood to reason that the same quality extended to the toybox.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hissabeth and I entered the box to verify this theory.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: With its stabilizing core gone, the environment in the toybox has also become affected by its observers. In fact, we found the level of chaos is positively correlated to the number of observers.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Observer effect, changing environment ...

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Familiar, isn't it? Our current situation seems to share many qualities with Artificial Somnambulism.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hissabeth has gone to get reinforcements. Hm, right on time.
Just as Pointer had estimated, Hissabeth leads Mesmer Jr. into the meeting room.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Go on, time's precious!
Hissabeth steps back. Mesmer Jr. approaches the toybox.
She leans over, peering down at the small, almost real "world" inside.
A textbook "zoo hypothesis."

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I'm sorry, but this isn't the same as Artificial Somnambulism.
After a long pause, she delivers her verdict.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I don't come to this conclusion arbitrarily. I've been paying attention to your experiments on this toybox.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Look.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: In your toybox, there's still a vending machine at the entrance to the Laplace laboratories.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: It's true! But out here, that vending machine was removed two days ago.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Artificial Somnambulism creates images based on subconscious memory. It's blurry and malleable. Even with our guidance, memories can still lie to you.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: That's why we use it primarily for psychotherapy, not simulations for experiments.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: It's likely this toybox is operating on a set formula based on the environmental conditions that were initially loaded, making it unable to generate things not included in its original data set.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Although your observations have turned into a chaotic mess for the time being, it has no inherent ability to change to reflect the real world.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: That is to say, the data in the toybox is from a static point in the past. If you don't update it, the vending machine will stay.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: It's this lag in data that gives it stability.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: That's the best I can offer.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: No, your conclusion was very valuable. So it's clear. If we want to progress, there's only one way left.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Return the core to the tower and let the toybox restabilize. Then reset it to stop this entropy and return it to its original state.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You mean, we regenerate the outer layer of the core to create a combination lock that can easily be analyzed?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Correct. Considering the chaos in the toybox, this mission should fall to you and Ulrich.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You two are the most familiar with its environment.
Field, Toybox
The all too familiar field of grass appears once more.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Why is our starting point always set here?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: It seems the toybox is more stable than we expected.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The topography hasn't changed at all, although we have lost line of sight to the tower.
Ulrich looks to the horizon. The tower's spire, once faintly visible, is now swallowed by heavy clouds.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Don't worry, we've already located the tower.
Through the device, Hissabeth's slightly distorted voice brings them their second piece of good news.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Although there have been some slight changes, it still remains northeast of where you are.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Just go ahead. We'll sync with your current position and route.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Oh, but can we assume that syncing our data out here won't trigger the observer effect?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Let's go.
Confirming that the core is safe inside the container, he shoulders the weight.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Please record the time intervals between the toybox's environmental changes.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Data's already been synced.
The two researchers wordlessly move northeast.
It seems they have both tacitly chosen silence as their safest option.
For a while, the communicator is the only thing making any sound.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Enigma, Ulrich, the data is starting to fluctuate.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: The observer effect will most likely begin manifesting soon. Prepare yourselves.
They halt. A bubble-like barrier drifts across the plain.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh! This is like a development on the Rorschach test.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I can hardly wait to see what scenes might appear.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: How did we end up here?
In the blink of an eye, the plain is gone, and they find themselves at the edge of a lake.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Environmental changes took 15 minutes this time. No change in the direction of the tower. Sure looks like a nice fishing spot you've ended up in.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ah. As if we didn't have enough problems, a lake?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What, do we have to row a boat now?!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I have no particular fondness for natural environments. I think this one's on you, Adler.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Good to see you've finally grasped the most important skill of social interaction—shifting blame.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The last time I visited a lake was before I joined Laplace.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Admit it, Ulrich! You're curious about them!

items.speaker: Ulrich & Enigma
items.text: What happened?!
Their argument is cut short. Like a television switched off, they are plunged into complete darkness.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: The data's becoming more volatile. The toybox is losing control.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: At least the communicator's still working.
Enigma feels around inside his backpack and pulls out the core.
It has warped violently inside its frame, looking nothing like it did before.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Which direction is the tower?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It's moved. Current position, unclear.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: There's no easy way ahead for now, so we'll make a temporary stop here. Check the position again after the next cycle of environmental changes.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Wait, Adler.
The darkness has sharpened their hearing. There's a rustling closing in from all sides.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Looks like we'll have to deal with this first.

items.speaker: X
items.text: You two alright? We've got the data. The tower's new location—it's extremely close to your position!

items.speaker: X
items.text: Wait, that's not right. It's ON your position.
The "projector" fast-forwards again, tossing them into the next frame.
Tower, Toybox

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Yes, we're under the tower.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That certainly saved us some effort.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Hmm. If the toybox's environment is affected by its observers' thoughts, then did we arrive here so quickly because our goals completely aligned with one another?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: How about that! A wish-granter and psychoanalysis machine all wrapped into one!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: This would work wonders for my survey on arcane skills!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Right, let's get the core into the tower and prepare our next steps.
Just as they reach for the tower door, a shrill cry splits the air.
A raven swoops down from nowhere, snatching the container in its beak and flying into the distance.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Ludwig?! Why is he still here?!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Damn it! X, can you follow Ludwig's trail?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: He's made off with the core!

items.speaker: X
items.text: Not a problem. We've got his arcane fluctuations on record! Just hold for a moment.
The communicator hisses with static.

items.speaker: X
items.text: A few seconds later, the answer comes through.

items.speaker: X
items.text: The tracking data's been interrupted. We lost him after about 50 meters of flight.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Mr. Ludwig has left. Or, more specifically, disappeared.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Huh. This is residual da ... System error?

items.speaker: X
items.text: It'd be best if you ... interrupt ... evacuate as quickly as possible ...
Enigma ignores his pleas, which are now reduced to static. Jaw clenched, he pushes hard against the tower door.
It doesn't budge.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: ... Already ... forced restart ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hmm?
A metal object lies on the ground in a spot he hadn't noticed before.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Greta's badge? She really came all the way here?
He reaches for it without thinking.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Researcher Adler!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: They've issued the force quit alert! No matter what you see, don't approach it. We have to avoid interfering with the data.
Ulrich grabs Enigma by the collar, yanking him off balance.
The mystery of the badge goes unsolved. Their bodies begin to disintegrate into pixels.
Finally, he is pulled from the space. The tower collapses into a cone of light and disappears.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But—
